newsitem.title: CANADA: Some Minorco Manitoba workers favor deal.
newsitem.headline: Some Minorco Manitoba workers favor deal.

text.p: A majority of the workers at Minorco SA's Hudson Bay Mining and Smelting Co Ltd in northern Manitoba voted in favor of a new collective agreement, a company spokeswoman said on Wednesday.
But the new contract offer was still in limbo since one trade union representing about 45 workers rejected the offer, the spokeswoman said.
Workers represented by the United Steelworkers, the biggest union at the zinc and coopper operation, voted about 63 percent for the agreement, the company said.
A group of unions voted 73 percent for the contract. But one union -- representing 45 boilermakers -- rejected the offer by a vote of 55 percent, the company said.
The company had yet to decide what to do about the vote split, the spokeswoman said.
About 250 workers represented by a mechanics' union have not voted on a new contract proposal. The union and the company will go to conciliation on March 4.
Company officials may wait until then to decide on their next step with the boilermakers, the spokeswoman said.
The last contract with the operation's 2,100 employees expired on October 1. Copper production from the smelter was 74,000 tonnes in 1995. Zinc production was 93,000 tonnes in 1995.
